When we process block operations we can deterministically check that these correspond to our view of the state and validate the block correctly if these withdrawals correspond to our validator set this gets rid of the entire queue from the state, what is the problem? Hmmm, I'll prepare a PR, I guess I'll only understand just then what's wrong https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3068 There must be something seriously wrong cause this is much simpler than the current implementation, but I can't really see something seriously wrong now. Ohhh c'mon Alex I saw you typing and I'm suffering now lol im thinking you want to do it "just in time" what i was typing: i don't exactly follow what is happening in this PR but i can say we have the queue to do what queues do: uncouple production from consumption of the queued object the idea is to let withdrawals accumulate at the CL, regardless of the EL's ability to process them yeah I imagine, but I don't see any danger in paying right now, the queue only delays it a few slots now plus you can't get out too much capital per block. i don't think there is a safety issue but e.g. if you have a bunch of missed slots, you could still get withdrawals into the queue and not have them blocked on getting a block on-chain there's no need for that if we have a sweep so either amortize this load across epoch processing sessions or you concentrate it all into block processing what exactly do you mean by sweep? #3042? Right, if you process every single validator the same way, and go looping through the validator registry 16 per slot, then you do not need to queue them. You still need to get your BLS_TO_EXECUTION message in a block. But your withdrawal will be automatically inserted sure This takes away a lot of the complexity and bloat from the beaconstate and can't seem to see anything seriously wrong with it well i do like having withdrawals directly committed to in the state so you can make stable proofs about them it should be the same if we did "just in time" and just adds a few extra hashes to go through the block root, so not end of hte world But the queue is ephemeral in the current implementation anyway taking a step back, i want to acknowledge that we can revisit the overall design but i personally feel it is a bit late in the process given everything else the client devs as team want to implement in the next 6 months the problem with the queue that I am seeing in my own implementation is memory fragmentation, it's not nice to have a queue changing every 12 seconds. If 3024 passes then we can make that queue into a circular buffer of fixed size, that is much better, but no queue at all is way better for us it feels like the kind of thing where the entity that wants to re-open the design process needs to get broad support from those who would bear the cost before going down this road just to play devil's advocate, it seems like you could implement it this way and just have some special logic to hammer the state computation into the spec as-is I was afraid that I was going to get this, however there's something wrong with the whole Ethereum development cycle if it happens like this. EF research proposes something, and we only see problems when we implement it. The merge happened about a month ago, we are now starting to implement Withrawals and we immediately found two issues, that's why 3024 was born, and now I'm saying that it can be done actually in a much simpler way. We couldn't give feedback before because we weren't implementing it before. If it's always going to be late by the time we start implementing, then we would never have a saying in the process. and this is really unnacceptable To be fair, I'm not sure that we ever had broad support for the existing design. Seems that the general feeling was "we'll look at this after the merge", so isn't the right time to be looking at this right now? it seems like you have a say right now, we have an active discussion going across multiple forums -- the intention is not to crowd out your input, it just seems from my perspective that this change isn't unilaterally better; just another alternative in the design space i want client teams to chime in on the design here and if things were uniformly in one direction then i think we would all agree this is the way to go Ah then we are talking, I am happy to hear points against it and weigh them. From you I hear that you have the hability of making proofs against the state for withdrawals. I'd give the point that this feature, if ever used, requires you to have the state at that precise time since the queue is ephemeral and lasts only a few slots while with this design you know on chain that if a validator is withdrawable you know when it can be withdrawn (and if yuo force proposers to include the maximum number of withdrawals) then you know exactly when it was withdrawn. So with this proposal you can always give state proofs by proving that the validator was withdrawable at any given time yeah like i said i don't think the proof point is deal breaker the arguments in the PR are the more important ones -- the way we approach testing the spec, and the latency around validators waiting for withdrawn value i think at this point, we should just discuss w/ everyone on the next CL spec call and if you want to bring #3068 as support for this design i'd also think about cleaning up the code some, i'll leave some comments on the PR Thanks a lot for this, yeah I left it as a minimal draft to test if it's viable. I'll tag <@680234424037670912> who's looking at this on Teku, <@688748669268132001> who was against 3024 but perhaps I can make him change mind here that now is a much simpler implementation for us. And <@654267572107083777>, <@607055410104500244> but I don't know who's looking in Nimbus/LightHouse. Already tagged the prysm team, not sure what they'll say <@755590043632140352> one point to consider is that having a materialized queue in the state simplifies the block building code for validators I'm still really put off by the extra delay on withdrawals caused by 3024 been the one working on withdrawals for Nimbus so far yeah otherwise you need to do the validator set scan at block building time, rather than having it already be done ahead of time when processing the chain yeah, this was one of the things that came while thinking this problem. But the loop to find 16 withdrawable validators is farily trivial and cheap. The nasty case is if the chain is having a leaking time but I haven't looked at the edge cases that closely yet But notice that this scan doesn't really happen in real life: unless the chain has been leaking for a couple of weeks, you find your next validators immediately. It's true that if the chain is leaking for weeks then it takes time, but even this is better since each client can optimize this as they see fit instead of having the state dictating their behavior yes and to make the point, that's why we want a queue 🙂 have a working, naive implementation per consensus spec tests, not thrilled about two loops, with loop mechanics that aren't trivial to merge with other steps both for spec test structure and more intrinsic (the rotating-base-queue) reasons Just reading your comments in the PR <@539495253418180618> thankful for them 🙏. Have a question though: you want to keep the withrawal index in the `Withrawal` object so that this will be an increasing counter of how many withdrawals have been there already? If so, do you want me to keep track of this index in the beacon state as well and check against it on block processing? Perhaps I just got this point. Yeah, certainly we will cache a queue all the time. However this will be done in our terms, it doesn't need to be tested, it's not in the state, and most importantly it will have constant size 16, so it'll be a circular buffer the idea is it is a nonce, so even if you had two otherwise duplicate withdrawals, each withdrawal will be unique — and the intent is this facilitates tracking them off-chain sounds good, does it need to be tracked also on the Beacon? I suppose it does otherwise it's useless to keep it in the message 🙂 alright will make that change and i think from a safety perspective, your claims actually argue for a reified queue in the state “done on our terms” => now 5+ impls to track/test vs 1 “doesn’t need to be tested” => yes it does, and now the effort is duplicated in an ad-hoc fashion across each client, rather than have a unified approach that all testing energy can concentrate on and if we could make the queue in the state a circular buffer if that’s a sticking point we can have the queue in the state as is and clients can still implement as a circular buffer yeah, the state has to live somewhere and it has to be under consensus not at all: we test our own implementations, we have spectests to check that they agree, we do not need to include fields in the beaconstate just to make it easier that we all implement the same thing yes, this is my last comment in 3024, if we go with that approach, then the queue better be a circular buffer of fixed size, that would make that approach much easier. But no queue at all is much better the no queue approach removes completely the logic of `withdraw_balance` and epoch transition... epoch transition is always a touchy thing for clients. Not having any changes there seems like a big win yeah and i’m saying you can leverage the testing work done for all clients in your client or we can fracture the energy across distinct implementations, if you don’t see the value then i won’t be able to convince you I do see the value in spectests to test that we agree on our implementation. The forkchoice spectests have saved my neck many many times of making huge mistakes. But I certainly do not see the value in having an object in the beaconstate that will require a hardfork to take out if we decide to change that design for the sole purpose of testing equal behavior <@554799849288105986> has been working on it for lighthouse, but I am interested in the discussion so I'll try to catch up Ah nice, curious what Mark would say And you of course yes, we should not put it in unless we think it will stay there indefinitely So the current capella specs don't seem to specify how `bls_to_execution_change`'s get included in a block.. no mention of them being gossiped or incentivized to include.. Are you supposed to wait until you propose a block to include them locally? I had discussed not needing any queue and just processing per slot, but <@340345049063882753> and i ended up settling on minimal adjustments to make the idea less controversial. In terms of <@688748669268132001> being put off by the extra delay, that's on me, I only read the spec on the Monday of devcon, and for that I apologise, but I don't think that's a fantastic reason to avoid rationalising things a bit... Several people did say they didn't like the loop but it was easier to just implement, I'm not sure that's a place we want to be in either if there's alternatives that are objectively simpler... I think there was a discussion about adjusting balances for the entire epoch being potentially an issue, the state changes a lot more.. it'd certainly make things a little clearer than a buffer... I agree with the concept of the buffer only needing to be small rather than 2^40, but it'd at least need to cope with a few epochs of buffering when things go south if we continue to have a buffer... Ultimately I raised the PR for discussion, and I'm not 100% set on that as a solution if there's good alternatives. I'm back
